- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks by 15–30%.
- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 10–25% to align with true volatility.
- Model often overshoots after sentiment spikes (e.g., 1.00), especially in early 30d horizon — cap forecast at 1.2x historical max for that sentiment window.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d forecasts — if forecast is >2.5x recent 7d average, reduce by 20–40% unless sentiment is bullish.
- Horizon-specific: 30d forecasts are prone to overreacting to 1–2 day sentiment shifts — apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to forecast if sentiment volatility >0.25.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows, model tends to lag — add 0.1–0.3 to forecast for each 1.00 sentiment shift in the prior 5 days.
